To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ethanol and its metabolite acetate have different effects on hepatocytes, including gene expression and histone H3 hyper-acetylation, in part due to differences in the activation of the mitogen-activated kinase (MAPK) pathway and histone acetylation mechanisms.

1) ethanol, but not its major metabolite, acetate, induced histone H4 acetylation in hepatocytes, 2) ethanol-induced histone H3 and H4 acetylations were dependent on the reactive species and mitogen activated protein kinase pathways, 3) ethanol and acetate differentiably activated mRNA expression for various genes in hepatocytes, and 4) acetate inhibited histones deacetylase (HDAC) activity.
the effects of ethanol and its major metabolites, acetate and acetaldehyde, on histone H3 and H4 acetylation and on histone deacetylation are different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of histonine acetylation in rat primary hepatocytes.
the mechanisms of ethanol-induced gene expression in liver and its implications in alcoholic liver disease.
the mechanism of histones H3 and H4 acetylation and the role of this posttranslational modification of histones in the gene expression in hepatocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ethanol induces histone H3 hyperacetylation in rat hepatocytes through a mechanism that involves the generation of reactive oxygen species and the activation of the mitogen-activated kinase pathway.
ethanol and its metabolite acetate differentially affect hepatocytes in gene regulation, P-H2A levels, and the mechanisms of histone acetylation.

ethanol and acetates have distinct effects on histone acetylation and the mechanism of acetylation in hepatocytes, and that ethanol has a greater effect than acetate in increasing histone H3 and P-H2AX acetylation, increasing CYP2E protein, and increasing PNPLA3 expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ethanol and its major metabolites, acetate and acetaldehyde, have different actions in liver, and these actions are mediated via different pathways.

ethanol induces histone H3 hyperacetylation via the generation of reactive oxygen species and activation of MAPK pathway, and that acetate induces histone H2B hyperacetylation, and both ethanol and acetate activate histone H3 and H2B acetylation via the inhibition of histone deacetylation.
